headline: 7Y special CGB clears at 1.40%; CGB 10Y hits a 1-year low of 1.589% but CDB lags, spread back to 10.9bp
summary: A quiet, low-volume session extended Tuesday's rebound at the 10-year point only: the CCDC 10-year fell 1.6bp to 1.589%, its lowest close in a year, while the 30-year eased 0.3bp to 2.054% and the 2–7Y sector was flat to 0.2bp lower. The 10-year therefore led and the curve flattened, with 5s10s down to 25.6bp and 2s10s to 35.9bp, a 1-year low. Policy banks lagged: CDB 10-year rose 0.6bp to 1.698%, widening its spread over CGB to 10.9bp from 8.7bp, and ADBC and EXIM 10-year rose 0.7bp, while short and 5–7Y policy banks edged 0.1–1.5bp lower.
drivers: The MoF sold the RMB150bn second tranche of the bank-recapitalisation special CGB at a 1.40% coupon, about 4bp below the CCDC 7-year at 1.439% before the auction. The clearing level showed banks and insurers still absorbing supply that fund sellers will not, and pulled the 10-year down to a 1-year low.
Funds keep selling financial bonds; policy banks lag

Funds sold over RMB510bn of cash bonds in the past two weeks, mostly credit and financial paper, while large banks and insurers bought, per Cailian. That left CDB, ADBC and EXIM 10-year 0.6–0.7bp higher as CGBs rallied, re-widening the CDB 10Y spread by 2.2bp; the tax-exemption debate still weighs on policy banks more than on CGBs.

The PBOC drained a net RMB13.8bn through overnight reverse repos at 1.25% after a RMB254bn injection on Tuesday, and DR001 held near 1.30%. With the overnight rate now the policy anchor, the front end stays pinned: 1–3Y CGBs moved less than 1bp.
Yuan firm, stocks mixed and thin

The PBOC set the strongest yuan fixing since July 2022 as APEC opened in Shenzhen, and spot held near 6.67 per dollar. The STAR 50 rose 2.2% but A-share turnover fell to a 16-month low, so the stock-bond seesaw was muted; foreign investors added RMB39.5bn of CGBs in October, a sixth monthly rise.
data: +RMB39.5bn to RMB2.08tn; sixth monthly rise, largest since May
Steady haven buying supports CGBs over policy banks and helps the strong yuan.
Industrial output 4.8% y/y (f 5.3%, p 5.5%); retail sales 0.4% (f 0.8%, p 1.1%); FAI YTD −8.1% (f −7.0%, p −7.2%); property investment −21.6%
Broad miss with collapsing investment supports lower yields and the case for more fiscal and monetary support.
Smallest annual fall in 11 months but monthly declines persist, so no lift to credit demand yet.
New loans −RMB100bn (f +RMB20bn, p +RMB1.08tn); TSF RMB1.15tn (f 1.42tn, p 3.55tn); M2 7.1% (f 7.2–7.3%, p 7.2%); M1 4.4% (p 3.2%)
Record-low 4.7% loan growth confirms weak private demand and supports lower yields.
Strong external demand trims the growth-scare case for bonds and triggered mild profit-taking.
Soft household demand keeps the easing bias intact and supports low long-end yields.
Energy-driven cost push that squeezes margins rather than signalling demand; bonds looked through it.
view: Mildly bullish for the next 1–2 weeks, with the 10-year expected in a 1.56–1.62% CCDC range. The long from 1.628% is 3.9bp in the money and 0.9bp from the 1.58% target, so I trail the stop to 1.62% rather than add at a 1-year low; weak October activity and credit, a well-bid 7-year auction and steady foreign buying support the trend, but fund redemptions keep moves choppy. On the curve I stay in the 5Y-into-10Y flattener and prefer CGBs over policy banks until fund selling of financial bonds fades; CDB 10Y at 12bp over CGB is the level to switch back. A renewed redemption wave, a formal plan to tax bond interest, or DR001 holding above 1.35% would push the 10-year back above 1.62%; an LPR cut on Friday or a weak November PMI would take it toward 1.56%.

buckets.name: CGB 1–2Y
buckets.why: The 2-year is flat at 1.230% (7th percentile, average 1.301%) and the 1-year 1.176%, little changed all week. DR001 near 1.30% against the 1.25% overnight policy rate leaves no carry case for chasing the front end at these levels.
buckets.call: Hold; add 2-year CGBs only above 1.27%, or if DR001 settles back toward 1.25%.

buckets.name: CGB 5–7Y belly
buckets.why: 2s5s10s is −15.3bp (8th percentile, average −8.0bp), so the 5-year at 1.333% stays rich. The 5s10s flattener from ~29bp is at 25.6bp (34th percentile, average 26.6bp), 0.6bp from target after the 10-year led today; the 7-year special CGB at 1.40% shows the belly is well bid, so I lock in gains rather than add.
buckets.call: Keep the 5s10s flattener from ~29bp, target 25bp; stop tightened to 28bp from 31bp.

buckets.name: CGB 10Y
buckets.why: The 10-year fell 1.6bp to 1.589%, a 1-year low (1st percentile, average 1.753%), so the long from 1.628% is 3.9bp in the money. After outperforming, it is no longer cheap against neighbours: 7s10s20s is −29.9bp (45th percentile, average −29.5bp), down from the 71st percentile on Tuesday.
buckets.call: Long 10-year CGBs from ~1.628%, target 1.58%, stop trailed to 1.62% from 1.66%.

buckets.name: CGB 30Y
buckets.why: The 30-year eased only 0.3bp to 2.054% and TL futures rose 0.08%, so 10s30s steepened to 46.5bp (53rd percentile, average 46.0bp), right at its average. 30s50s is 11.1bp (6th percentile), so the ultra-long end offers little; insurer and year-end demand should still cap yields near 2.10%.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add above 2.10% (10s30s ~48bp); poor risk/reward below 2.03%.

buckets.name: Policy banks 2–10Y vs CGB
buckets.why: The CDB 10-year spread over CGB widened 2.2bp to 10.9bp (61st percentile, average 9.7bp) as funds kept selling financial bonds, close to but not at the 12bp entry. At 2Y policy banks stay at a 1-year tight (CDB 11.3bp, 0th percentile), so any value is at 7–10Y, not the front.
buckets.call: Buy CDB 10Y vs CGB 10Y at 12bp or wider, target 9bp, stop 15bp; avoid 1–3Y policy banks.

buckets.name: Policy banks 5–7Y vs CGB
buckets.why: The CDB 7-year spread over CGB is 19.5bp (73rd percentile, average 15.8bp), little changed after Monday's stop at 20.9bp, and ADBC 7Y is 18.8bp (98th percentile). The tax repricing keeps the tenor cheap, but fund selling of financial bonds has not eased, so I wait for a wider entry.
buckets.call: Flat; re-enter CDB 7Y vs CGB 7Y at 23bp+, target 18bp, stop 26bp.

buckets.name: ADBC/EXIM vs CDB 10Y
buckets.why: ADBC 10-year yields 2.0bp more than CDB (60th percentile, average 1.4bp) and EXIM 1.1bp (13th percentile, average 2.0bp); all three moved together today. ADBC's recent taps drew 3.6–4.9 times cover, so the extra pickup is not a demand problem.
buckets.call: Hold ADBC 10Y over CDB 10Y; switch back to CDB if the pickup falls below 1bp. Avoid EXIM 10Y at about 1bp.

buckets.name: Policy banks 20–30Y
buckets.why: The CDB 20-year spread over CGB is 9.8bp (55th percentile, average 10.3bp), unchanged on the day and near where I closed the CGB-over-CDB 20Y trade at ~9.5bp. The CDB 30-year spread is 11.0bp, a 1-year tight (average 12.5bp), so long policy banks offer no value.
buckets.call: Flat; re-enter CGB 20Y over CDB 20Y below 7bp; avoid CDB 30Y at an 11bp spread.
